name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,811

entries.clue: Live cheaply, putting millions into unfinished screenplay (6)

indicatorNotes.putting: you put one thing into another
indicatorNotes.into: tells you where the millions go
indicatorNotes.unfinished: the last letter of the word is missing

blocks.note: SCRIPT without its last letter
m = million(s)

annotation.surface: A struggling writer lives on very little while money pours into a half-written film script.
annotation.walkthrough: The M goes between SCRI and P. The irony is that millions go into the word for living cheaply.
annotation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to live cheaply, saving every penny.

entries.clue: Charlie lists recent record that's perfect (5,5)

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
a ship lists = leans to one side
late = recent, as in 'the late news'

annotation.surface: Someone called Charlie keeps lists of a recent flawless record, perhaps in sport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lists' looks like a noun or a verb for writing things down; it is the verb for a ship tilting.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a slate wiped clean carries no chalk marks, so a record without blemishes is a clean slate.

entries.clue: Written with feet upside down (7)

blocks.note: poems are measured in metrical feet, so this means written in rhyme and metre
turned the other way up, reversed

annotation.surface: It sounds like a strange scene of someone writing with their feet while standing on their head.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN VERSE is 'written with feet'; as one, INVERSE means turned over. 'Feet' are not the ones you stand on but units of rhythm.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for one sense: an inverse position is upside down; the other sense is the phrase in verse.

entries.clue: Play African country in pongy ground (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: PONGY rearranged, then split PYG...ON
Mali is a West African country

annotation.surface: Someone is told to play a game about an African country on a patch of smelly ground.
annotation.walkthrough: Pongy is British slang for smelly, and 'ground' means crushed, not a patch of earth. Pygmalion is the George Bernard Shaw play behind My Fair Lady.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Pygmalion is one well-known play, by Shaw.

entries.clue: Scratch and doodle? (8)

blocks.note: with = and, as in 'bread with butter'
to doodle is to draw idly

annotation.surface: Scratching and doodling, like someone idly marking paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratch' looks like a mark on paper; here it means pulling out of a race or contest.
annotation.definitionFit: A racing sense: a horse scratched from a race is taken out before the start.

entries.clue: Critical wife, seeing wee in your cups? (7)

blocks.note: w = wife, a standard abbreviation
as = seeing (that), since
a slurred drunk says PISS as PISH; in your cups = drunk

annotation.surface: A disapproving wife sees her drunken partner has wet himself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In your cups' is an old phrase for drunk, and the drunk's lisp turns the rude word for wee into PISH.
annotation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply critical or irritable.

entries.clue: Couple in Glasgow starts to notice ghastly local intonation (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starting letter of each following word

blocks.note: twa is Scots for two
first letters of notice and ghastly

annotation.surface: Someone in Glasgow notices a couple speaking with a dreadful local accent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Glasgow' tells you to use the Scots word for the couple.
annotation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive regional accent or intonation.

entries.clue: Make sense of cold, recently-emptied department stores (7)

indicatorNotes.recently-emptied: the word loses its insides, keeping only the ends
indicatorNotes.stores: the outer word keeps the others inside it

blocks.note: the usual short form of department
c = cold, as on a tap
RECENTLY with the middle removed

annotation.surface: Trying to understand the chilly shops that have lately been cleared out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Department stores' reads as big shops; split the phrase and the department's short form stores the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: you make sense of a coded message by decrypting it.

entries.clue: Top copy that's wrong (4)

blocks.note: to ape is to copy
X is the mark for a wrong answer

annotation.surface: A teacher marks a best piece of copying as wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top copy' reads as the top sheet of a document; split it into definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the highest point of a mountain or triangle is its top.

entries.clue: Avengers shot invisible weapon (5,3)

indicatorNotes.shot: shot = ruined, broken, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: The Avengers superheroes fire an invisible weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like firing, fitting the superheroes; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical weapon that cannot be seen.

entries.clue: German city first in alphabet, with long name (6)

blocks.note: A comes first in the alphabet
to long for = to ache for
n = name

annotation.surface: A German city that comes first alphabetically and has a long name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the name; it is the verb, to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Charlemagne's old capital near the Belgian border is one German city.

entries.clue: More and more at home managed care alone (12)

indicatorNotes.managed: managed = handled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: at home = in
CARE rearranged
singly = one by one, alone

annotation.surface: More and more often, care at home is managed single-handed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Managed care' reads as a health-policy term; here managed is the signal to rearrange CARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something that grows by degrees, more and more, does so increasingly.

entries.clue: Spontaneous date started with pre-nup Tom prepared (10)

indicatorNotes.started: only the start of date is used
indicatorNotes.prepared: prepared = made ready, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of date
the letters to rearrange, with D

annotation.surface: A spur-of-the-moment date began with Tom having a prenuptial agreement drawn up.
annotation.walkthrough: A pre-nup is a prenuptial agreement signed before a wedding; the surface's oddity is a spontaneous date that needs one.
annotation.definitionFit: Unprompted means spontaneous, done without being asked.

entries.clue: Chimney went overhead, you'd say (4)

blocks.note: flew = went overhead, as a bird

annotation.surface: Something flew over the chimney, as you might put it.
annotation.walkthrough: FLEW and FLUE are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: the smoke passage inside a chimney stands for the whole chimney.

entries.clue: Before long, insect bites hotel resident (10)

indicatorNotes.bites: what bites takes something into its mouth, so it contains it

blocks.note: in a bit = before long
Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet
the usual insect

annotation.surface: Soon an insect will bite a guest staying in a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotel resident' reads as a guest; the definition is just 'resident'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who lives in a place is its resident.

entries.clue: See one retail outlet in short block (9)

indicatorNotes.in: one part goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.short: the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: BRICK without its last letter
one = I, the Roman numeral
a shop is a retail outlet

annotation.surface: Look at a single shop squeezed into a small block of buildings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look; it is the noun, a bishop's diocese, and so is bishopric.
annotation.definitionFit: A see is the district a bishop rules, his bishopric.

entries.clue: Amazing biro, say, pocketed by academic without one (10)

indicatorNotes.pocketed by: the pen is put inside the other word
indicatorNotes.without: the named letter is taken out

blocks.note: studious = academic, bookish
one = I, removed to leave STUDOUS
a biro is a ballpoint pen; 'say' marks an example

annotation.surface: An amazing ballpoint slipped into the pocket of a lecturer who had none.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pocketed' pictures the pen slipping into a pocket; it signals one word going inside another. A biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something so great it astonishes you is amazing.

entries.clue: E.g. John Paul I and II taking mass in Italian city (7)

indicatorNotes.taking: the word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: John Paul I was a pope; 'e.g.' marks an example
m = mass in physics
the numeral II is added on

annotation.surface: Two popes of the same name celebrate mass in an Italian city.
annotation.walkthrough: POPE takes in M to give POMPE, then II is added. 'Mass' looks like the church service the popes would say; it is the physics symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: Pompeii is the Roman city near Naples buried by Vesuvius.

entries.clue: Keeping watch, running aground (2,5)

indicatorNotes.running: running = in motion, so its letters move about

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A lookout keeps watch while the ship runs aground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running aground' is a set phrase for a ship hitting bottom; running is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom from fencing: a fencer in the ready stance is alert and watchful.

entries.clue: Restrain dog beginning to bark (4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the beginning of the next word

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
first letter of bark

annotation.surface: Hold the dog back as it starts to bark.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plain instruction to a dog owner.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from riding: the chain on a bridle that holds a horse back was a curb.

entries.clue: 3D image of queen, say, on throne (3,4)

blocks.note: a queen is a female cat; 'of' makes it the possessive CAT'S
throne and can are both slang for the toilet

annotation.surface: A three-dimensional picture of a monarch seated on her throne.
annotation.walkthrough: The queen is a female cat and the throne is a lavatory, so the royal portrait is a cat's toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A CAT scan builds cross-sectional X-ray images into a 3D view of the body.

entries.clue: Repair faulty item quickly near destination (4,4,4)

annotation.definitionNote: Neither half is a clean verb phrase: the first is a cryptic hint at mending a clock, the second describes arriving quickly.

blocks.note: fix a faulty clock so it keeps accurate hours
travellers moving fast as they near the end of a journey

annotation.surface: Fix a broken item fast as you approach your destination.
annotation.walkthrough: The faulty item is a clock: to repair it is to make it keep good time.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a mended clock keeps accurate hours, and a journey that runs fast is quick progress.

entries.clue: A boat you can capsize? (5)

blocks.note: the definition: a small paddled craft
capsize the word, turning it back to front, and it reads the same

annotation.surface: Asking whether this boat is one you are able to tip over.
annotation.walkthrough: Capsizing turns a boat over; KAYAK is a palindrome, so flipping the word changes nothing. The question mark flags the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Kayaks are small boats, and paddlers practise rolling them over and back up.

entries.clue: Water area covered by turf (4)

indicatorNotes.covered by: in a down answer, one part sits beneath the other

blocks.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a = area

annotation.surface: A patch of water has been covered over with turf.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer the A sits under SOD.
annotation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: the fizzy mixer water in a whisky and soda is carbonated water.

entries.clue: Find humour when swapping sides in bed (4,2)

indicatorNotes.when swapping sides in bed: BED begins with B and ends with D; swap those sides so D becomes B

blocks.note: comedy = humour
the D is replaced by B, the other side of BED

annotation.surface: A couple find something funny when they swap sides of the bed.
annotation.walkthrough: COMEDY has a D; trading it for the B at the other end of BED gives COMEBY.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to get hold of something, as when you chance on a rare book, is to find it.

entries.clue: Crossing island, stop car unexpectedly for fruit (8)

indicatorNotes.Crossing: the letters go across the island, taking it inside
indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: the letters come in a surprising order

blocks.note: STOP CAR rearranged, split APR...COTS
i = island

annotation.surface: A driver crossing an island stops suddenly to buy fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop car' reads as an instruction to the driver; it is the letters to rearrange, and 'crossing' puts them either side of the island.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: small orange stone fruits from the rose family, like plums.

entries.clue: Old man under arrest became hysterical (8)

indicatorNotes.under: one part comes after the other

blocks.note: old man = father = pa
nicked is British slang for arrested

annotation.surface: An elderly man lost his nerve when he was arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Under arrest' is a set phrase; split it and 'under' puts the father first.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: losing control in a sudden fright is becoming hysterical.

entries.clue: Cold northern state has nothing on California (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, one part comes after the other

blocks.note: CA is California's postal code
nada is Spanish for nothing

annotation.surface: A cold northern state owes nothing to California.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface frames Canada against its warm southern neighbour.
annotation.definitionFit: Canada is a cold country in the far north of America.
